title: Solo founder lessons: shipping dead ideas, user calls, and loneliness
summary: Farza recounts a week where a shelved idea (Clicky) went viral while he felt lonely building solo. He explains why he ships stale ideas, values usage over views, calls top users to find direction, and assembles a small team rather than waiting for a co-founder.

principles.text: Don't let ideas rot on a shelf; ship them and see what happens.
principles.quote: I hate that feeling where it's like I feel like every idea should be just taken off the shelf and just thrown out into the world. And you just see what happens, you know?

principles.text: Usage matters, not virality or views.
principles.quote: views don't mean much to me. What mean What matters is like usage.

principles.text: When unsure, check top users in analytics and talk to them directly.
principles.quote: I looked at our top 25 users by usage um and I picked out 10 of them and I sent them all emails to my calendar and I said let's talk tomorrow.

principles.text: You can't predict who will use your product or why until it's out; let users reveal use cases.
principles.quote: As a founder, you have no freaking idea who's going to use your product and why they're going to use it until you put it out there.

principles.text: Treat user feedback as inspiration, not a spec to build one-to-one.
principles.quote: I just take feedback as inspiration. It's almost like I'm an LLM, and the users, when I talk to them, are prompting me.

principles.text: Drive forward yourself and let people join, rather than waiting for a co-founder.
principles.quote: I think that the best way to find people and to work with people is by just driving forward yourself. And as you drive forward, hopefully other people hop in your car as well
